checkup.title: Infant health and dental checkups
checkup.desc: Windows for the 8 infant health checkups and 4 dental checkups of the National Health Insurance Service (NHIS). A round cannot be taken once its window has passed.
checkup.note: '4–6 months' is counted from the day the baby turns 4 months to the day before 7 months. The NHIS guide does not spell out a date rule, so dates may differ by a day; confirm with the NHIS lookup.

support.title: National immunization support
support.eligible: Born on or after 2013-01-01, so your child is eligible for the 2026 children's national immunization program. Vaccines in the schedule above are free (vaccine and administration fees) at designated clinics and public health centers. See per-vaccine conditions below.
support.notEligible: Children born before 2013-01-01 are not eligible for the 2026 children's national immunization program (age 12 and under).
items: BCG (intradermal), Hib and pneumococcal vaccines are covered up to 59 months of age.
Rotavirus is covered up to 8 months 0 days, with dose 1 by 14 weeks 6 days.
HPV covers girls aged 12–17 (born 2008–2014) and boys aged 12 (born 2014, from 2026-05-06). Check the rules again when your child is 11–12.
High-risk children also receive pneumococcal vaccine at 24 months to 12 years.
Percutaneous BCG, the live Japanese encephalitis vaccine Imojev and 9-valent HPV are not part of the program and are paid out of pocket.
Support applies only at designated clinics and public health centers.

howTo.title: How to use
items: Enter the birth date and each cell of the KDCA 2026 standard schedule turns into dates for your child.
Pick the rotavirus product and the Japanese encephalitis vaccine type (inactivated or live).
Check off doses as they are given. Checked doses drop out of the next-dose calculation and are saved in this browser only.
Tap 'Add to calendar' to download an .ics file with the remaining doses and checkup start dates.

basis.title: How it is calculated
items: A '2 months' cell runs from the day the baby turns 2 months to the day before 3 months; '15–18 months' runs from 15 months to the day before 19 months.
Cells written as ages such as '4–6 years' use completed years (from the 4th birthday to the day before the 7th birthday).
If the month has no matching day (e.g. born on January 31), the last day of that month is used (Jan 31 + 1 month = Feb 28 or 29).
Where the table merges two doses into one cell ('doses 1–2' of hepatitis A, inactivated Japanese encephalitis and HPV), they are shown as one item with the interval from the KDCA disease pages.
Infant checkup 1 runs from day 14 to day 35; other rounds convert the NHIS month ranges to dates the same way.

care.title: Before and after · same-day shots
items: Before: a caregiver who knows the child's condition well should come along. Take the temperature at home to make sure there is no fever, and bathe the child the day before.
After: stay at the clinic for 20–30 minutes, then watch closely for at least 3 hours at home.
Pay special attention for at least 3 days and see a doctor right away for high fever or seizures.
Getting several vaccines on the same day is generally not a contraindication; decide with the screening doctor.
At 2, 4 and 6 months, combination vaccines such as DTaP-IPV/Hib (5-in-1) or DTaP-IPV-Hib-HepB (6-in-1) reduce the number of injections. Using the 6-in-1 can change the hepatitis B schedule.

items.q: If we missed a dose, do we have to start over?
items.a: KDCA notes that if doses are not given on the standard schedule, the schedule may change depending on age. For DTaP, polio, Hib, pneumococcal and inactivated Japanese encephalitis vaccines, delays can change the number of doses and intervals, so plan a catch-up schedule with the screening pediatrician. Rotavirus dose 1 is not started after 15 weeks 0 days, and the series must be finished by 8 months 0 days.

items.q: Can my baby get several vaccines on the same day?
items.a: KDCA's precautions and contraindications page says getting several vaccines at once is generally not a contraindication and that vaccination should follow a screening exam. At 2, 4 and 6 months, when 4–5 vaccines are due at once, combination vaccines reduce the number of injections.

items.q: What should I do if my baby has a fever after a shot?
items.a: Watch closely for at least 3 days and see a doctor right away for high fever or seizures (KDCA). If you give a fever reducer, follow the weight-based dose; you can check it with the Toolhub children's fever medicine dose calculator. If a baby under 3 months has a fever, see a doctor before giving medicine.

items.q: What about vaccines not in the schedule, such as meningococcal?
items.a: This tool covers only the national vaccines in the KDCA standard schedule. Meningococcal vaccine is recommended for high-risk groups such as complement deficiency or HIV infection and for travelers to endemic areas; it is not part of the national program, so it is paid out of pocket. Percutaneous BCG, the live Japanese encephalitis vaccine Imojev and 9-valent HPV are also paid out of pocket. Discuss them with your pediatrician.

items.q: Is the rotavirus vaccine 2 doses or 3?
items.a: It depends on the product. RV1 (Rotarix) is 2 doses at 2 and 4 months; RV5 (RotaTeq) is 3 doses at 2, 4 and 6 months. It is given by mouth and is covered up to 8 months 0 days, with dose 1 by 14 weeks 6 days.

Under the NHIS program there are 8 checkups from day 14–35 (round 1) to 66–71 months (round 8), plus 4 dental checkups at 18–29, 30–41, 42–53 and 54–65 months. A round cannot be taken once its window has passed, so put the start dates in your calendar. Confirm exact dates with the NHIS infant checkup date lookup.

items.q: Who gets national vaccinations for free?
items.a: As of 2026, children aged 12 and under (born on or after 2013-01-01) get the full cost of required vaccinations (vaccine and administration fees) covered at designated clinics and public health centers. BCG, Hib and pneumococcal vaccines are covered up to 59 months and rotavirus up to 8 months 0 days; HPV covers girls aged 12–17 and boys aged 12 (born 2014, from 2026-05-06).
